HydroAI is a deep-tech startup dedicated to water resources management through advanced Earth Observation and intelligent data processing. Born from scientific research and validated through international collaboration, the entity specializes in providing actionable intelligence for the monitoring and preservation of freshwater resources.
The core mission of HydroAI is to bridge the gap between complex environmental data and practical decision-making. The startup operates primarily in the downstream sector of the space economy, transforming raw satellite data into high-value information services. By focusing on the entire water cycle within reservoir and catchment systems, the entity addresses critical challenges such as water scarcity, drought resilience, and storage infrastructure integrity.
HydroAI’s service portfolio is designed to provide a broad view of water assets. This includes the continuous monitoring of water availability and surface extent, the assessment of water quality to safeguard ecosystem health, and the delivery of predictive insights to anticipate future water stress. Additionally, the startup offers specialized surveying capabilities to map the physical characteristics of water storage reservoir, ensuring that managers have an accurate understanding of their total capacity.
As a science-based venture, HydroAI acts as a strategic partner for the agricultural sector, public water authorities, and environmental agencies. By delivering clarity in an increasingly unpredictable climate, the startup empowers stakeholders to optimize irrigation, improve resource allocation, and implement sustainable governance strategies. Currently supported by leading impact incubators and recognized in innovation competitions, HydroAI is positioned at the forefront of digital transformation for rural and water-dependent communities.

With over 50 years of experience, we position ourselves as an innovative and committed engineering consultancy, providing an integrated and sustainable approach to meet the current and future demands of our sector.

LSC360 embodies an ambitious vision where 360° engineering means a holistic approach to each project, connecting skills and solutions to create a positive impact on society. Our core values—centered on well-being, empathy, and social responsibility—are at the heart of our approach. We firmly believe that the success of each project relies as much on high-performing technical solutions as on respecting human aspirations.

We have established our market position through the completion of major national and international projects, always guided by client satisfaction as our top priority.

Our social and environmental responsibility is reflected in the ESR (Socially Responsible Company) label, as well as ISO 14001 for environmental management and ISO 45001 for health and safety at work. Through our Integrated Management System (IMS), we ensure the monitoring and implementation of our actions in terms of quality, health, safety, and environment. We are also proud to carry the Made in Luxembourg label, a symbol of our expertise and local roots.
Thanks to advanced IT tools, continuous training, and the rigor of our teams, we guarantee the quality and precision of every plan and report. At LSC360, we combine expertise, innovation, and commitment to be a key player in the transformation toward a sustainable future.

Our mission is to support our clients in the realization of integrated projects of all scales, combining efficiency and empathy. Our vision is based on the union of diverse talents and engineering expertise to design, inspire, and shape a meaningful society.
Our core values are expressed through three main commitments:
360° Well-being: placing people, empathy, and community connection at the heart of our actions
360° Engineering: ensuring technical expertise and innovative solutions
360° Sustainability: embodying a global approach that integrates environmental, economic, and social responsibility

Earth Observation (EO) satellites are perfectly suited for the monitoring and the reporting of geopolitical events affecting the global economy and the well-being and security of millions of people (e.g., wars, humanitarian crises, energy crises, pandemics, supply chain disruptions…). Extracting geospatial intelligence from satellite imagery usually involves at least some degree of manual work by human image analysts. However, over the last few years the amount of available data has increased dramatically. This makes it practically impossible to effectively process all the available imagery through visual exploitation, thus increasing the need for software tools which can automatically extract actionable insights from the data.
TerraLens, a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), offers cutting edge solutions to exploit EO data for political and strategic decision making. We fill the gap between scientific prototyping and operational requirements by implementing state-of-the-art algorithms into professional software solutions for security-relevant applications. Our automatic monitoring solutions enable non-technical end-users to easily define their specific problem, analyze vast amounts of data with little effort, interact with the original data and the extracted insights, and take actions based on these insights.

entityDescription:
The Museo Galileo–Institute and Museum for the History of Science—born in 1925—is home to a world renowned collection of scientific instruments. Among the most exceptional are instruments that belonged to Galileo Galilei, including the only two surviving telescopes of the many that he built.
Museo Galileo is an institute for advanced research and documentation in the history of science and technology, offering scholars from across the world the great resources of its library and its website.
Museo Galileo routinely partners with such prestigious Italian and international institutions as the CNR-Italian Council for Research, Uffizi Galleries, Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei, Museo Archeologico Nazionale of Naples, Parco Archeologico del Colosseo, Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana in Venice, Laboratorio Europeo per la Spettroscopia Non Lineare (LENS), Royal Library at Windsor Castle, Max-Planck Society’s institutes, Harvard University, Dresden Staatliche Kunstsammlungen, and takes part in innovative research projects.
Deeply engaged in the dissemination of scientific culture, Museo Galileo organizes temporary exhibitions on the history of science and the interactions of science and technology with the arts, which are displayed in important venues both in Italy and abroad.
All Museo Galileo’s temporary exhibitions are the outcome of in-depth research carried out by scholars of great renown who are members or collaborators of the Florentine institution. Leonardo da Vinci’s work, Galileo’s astronomical discoveries, Medici and Lorrain collections, early modern cartography are among the subjects to whom Museo Galileo devoted its exhibitions. In addition, thanks to partnership with major archaeological museums, Museo Galileo’s produced a series of exhibitions dealing with scientific and technical knowledge in the Antiquity.

Zetarium is a Netherlands-based insurtech and agri-risk analytics company developing advanced probabilistic models for crop productivity, climate risk, and parametric insurance. Our platform integrates satellite Earth Observation, weather data, and statistical/AI-based uncertainty quantification to support insurers, governments, and financial institutions in designing transparent, scalable agricultural risk solutions.

We collaborate internationally across Europe and Central Asia to enable climate-resilient agriculture, improve access to insurance for farmers, and support evidence-based policy design. Zetarium’s work focuses on transforming EO data into operational decision-support tools, feasibility studies, and pilot implementations with public-benefit impact.

Zetarium delivers satellite‑enabled parametric insurance and market services that support financers and traders while strengthening agricultural resilience. The platform combines satellite imagery, meteorological feeds, and actuarial/risk models to automate loss detection and risk assessment and to supply data across the farming value chain.

The system replaces manual loss adjustment and traditional risk management with automated, auditable decisioning. Inputs from Earth observation and weather feeds are processed through actuarial and risk models to generate objective triggers and risk metrics that can be consumed by insurers, financiers, traders, and farm operators.

Zetarium produces standardized, auditable data products for claims triggers, portfolio risk assessment, and market decision support. These outputs are intended to inform underwriting, financing, trading, and on‑farm risk management across both smallholder and commercial contexts.

About Us
Ateleris GmbH is a privately owned Swiss engineering company headquartered in Brugg, Switzerland, specializing in software and data engineering for the space sector. Our space practice operates as SPACE by Ateleris (https://ateleris.space). Founded in 2016 as a spin-off from the FHNW Institute for Data Science, we build on more than a decade of applied R&D work for European space missions, with TRL 9 flight software operational in orbit on ESA's Solar Orbiter since 2020.
What we do
We engineer software end-to-end along the flow of data, from onboard instruments through ground pipelines to user-facing platforms:
Flight Software. Instrument and payload software, onboard AI and machine learning, custom file systems, TM/TC handling, EGSE test automation, commissioning, and long-duration operations support.
AI and Data Engineering. Science data pipelines from raw telemetry (L0) to science-ready products (L2+), archival systems, calibration workflows, HPC and cloud-native processing, and applied machine learning on ground and in orbit.
Platforms and Integration. Web platforms, dashboards, operator tools, and backend APIs that connect space systems, data, and users. User-centred design with stakeholder workshops and in-house security review.
Flight heritage
Ateleris is co-developer of the flight and ground software for STIX (Spectrometer/Telescope for Imaging X-rays) on ESA's Solar Orbiter, operational since February 2020. The automated STIX science pipeline has been running continuously since end of 2021. Team experience also spans RHESSI, Euclid, ARRAKIHS, SKA, SDO, and e-CALLISTO.
How we work
We cover the full software lifecycle (SRR, PDR, CDR, QR/AR) and work either fully ECSS-compliant when mission criticality demands it, or ECSS-informed for leaner research-driven projects. Our practice combines CCSDS and PUS-C heritage, formal verification with Stainless (Scala) and Viper (Python), CI/CD with digital twins, and applied machine learning on resource-constrained hardware.
Partners and memberships
Partners and clients include ESA, FHNW, armasuisse Science and Technology, the University of Bern, EPFL, and Paul Scherrer Institute, alongside prime contractors across Europe. Ateleris is a member of the Swiss Space Industries Group (SSIG) of Swissmem.

Founded in 1986, A.U.G. Signals Ltd. (AUG) has been dedicated to excellence in signal, image and data processing for over three decades. A leader in its field, AUG is at the forefront of research and development in registration, detection, recognition, classification and identification, tracking, data mining techniques, intelligent systems and online distributed processing, situation assessment for decision support, and multi-sensor information fusion.

AUG has an extensive track record of successful projects, collaborating with government, academic and industry partners. AUG develops customized technologies and products for its clients. The company has the capabilities to deliver end-to-end solutions (data acquisition, processing, map production and online distribution) that effectively meet clients’ specifications and unique requirements. A shortlist of activities include airborne hyperspectral surveys; the custom implementation of Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) systems for Automatic Target Detection (ATD), Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) and situation assessment and decision support; the custom implementation of Image Change Detection and Automatic Multi-sensor Image Registration and Fusion systems; and online signal processing. AUG is also active in processing a wide range of space-based, airborne, and ground-based applications.
